qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Regulated natural gas and electricity distribution concessions hold local natural monopoly positions in Spain and Latin America, but allowed returns are politically capped by the CNMC (financial remuneration rate ~5.58% for electricity distribution and ~5.44% for gas distribution). The merchant generation and energy supply divisions are price-takers in volatile wholesale electricity and LNG markets, exposed to state clawbacks (topes al gas) and windfall taxes. 5-year median GAAP ROIC is ~8% (ranging from 6.5% to 11.1%), failing the 12% hurdle, with no autonomous pricing power >= inflation.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (Proof of Moat & Pricing Power, REJECT). Spanish multi-utility with regulated gas and power networks and merchant generation. Regulated asset base remuneration is capped at ~5.5-6.5% by the CNMC, while merchant power and gas commercialization face wholesale price volatility, regulatory clawback interventions, and windfall taxes. Multi-cycle GAAP ROIC is sub-hurdle (~8%), lacking genuine pricing power >= inflation.
qualitative.evidence: Consolidated EBITDA hovered around €5.3B-€5.5B across 2023-2025 with net debt at €12.3B (~2.3x EBITDA). Historical reported ROIC stood at 6.5% in 2018 and averaged ~8-9% over the 2018-2024 strategic plan, only briefly reaching 11.1% in 2024 and 11.3% in 2025 during elevated European gas/power sparks, well short of the 12% cycle-neutral hurdle. Shifting shareholder dynamics (CriteriaCaixa, CVC, GIP, IFM) and aborted split plans (Project Gemini) reflect ongoing strategic and regulatory frictions.
